title: Special Executive Masters Programme in Project Management
description: The Special Executive Masters Programme (SEMP) in Project Management equips professionals with cutting-edge methodologies and leadership skills to drive successful project execution and strategic innovation.
university: The Global School of Skills (GSS) and Rushford Business School
longDescription: The Special Executive Masters Programme (SEMP) in Project Management offers advanced training in innovative project methodologies and strategic leadership tailored for senior professionals. This program empowers participants to efficiently lead complex projects and drive organizational success through cutting-edge management techniques. The Programme offers an efficient approach beyond traditional classroom learning. The course emphasises real-world applications through case studies, business simulations, and 100% project-based learning, allowing participants to practice what they learn in a controlled environment before applying it to their roles. The Special Executive Master Programme in Project Management allows you to achieve the qualification in 6 months. It is a fast track to new opportunities and enhanced career prospects. The program effectively prepares learners to tackle complex operational challenges by integrating theoretical knowledge with practical applications.
courseDetails: The aim of the Special Executive Masters Programme (SEMP) in Project Management is to equip executives with advanced skills in strategic planning, execution, and leadership to drive successful project outcomes. The program emphasizes innovative methodologies and decision-making techniques to enhance efficiency and foster sustainable growth in dynamic environments. Course Details: Planning, Controlling, and Leading a Project: Provides learners with the expertise to strategize, monitor, and guide projects to successful completion. Procurement Risk and Contract Management: Emphasizes risk mitigation and optimization of procurement processes through effective contract management. Advanced Project and Logistics Management: Delves into advanced techniques to enhance efficiency and streamline project and logistics operations. Operations and Information Management for Project Managers: Offers insights into managing project operations and information flow for seamless execution. Advanced Research Methods: Enhances proficiency in research methodologies critical for project analysis, decision-making, and innovation. Assessment: Graduation Project (GP) After completing the coursework, students must complete a graduation project (GP) integrating knowledge from all modules. This project assesses their ability to apply current practices in Project management and solidifies their comprehensive understanding of the field. Programme Structure and Credits: This programme comprises five modules with 30 ECTS and 1 GP of 30 ECTS.

modules.title: PLANNING, CONTROLLING AND LEADING A PROJECT
modules.summary: This unit aims to introduce learners to the realities of developing and managing a project. It will also introduce learners to the challenges of project management practice in the global business arena. It aims to promote thinking critically about project management as complex, process-based cultural systems and as constantly developing with the high performing team efforts. As an increasing number of firms have project development and project management activities, understanding efficient project management is of vital importance. Learners will learn about the roles and responsibilities of project team members. Various level of management skills will be studied with a special focus on success factors, monitoring and control.

modules.title: PROCUREMENT RISK AND CONTRACT MANAGEMENT
modules.summary: The aim of the unit is to enable the student to understand the core concepts of procurement along with the importance of identifying and managing risks related to procurement and contract management. The learners will also develop a critical understanding of various legislative frameworks important for procurement and consider frameworks for risk assessment in the procurement context.

modules.title: ADVANCED PROJECT AND LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT
modules.summary: The aim of this unit is to allow the learner to understand concepts of portfolio management and its associated features. The value of having a Project Management Office will also be examined, and the stages of establishing an effective project management office will be considered. Learners will also examine the supply chain ecosystem and review IT frameworks appropriate for logistics and supply chain complexities.

lessons.title: Concepts in Global Supply Chain Ecosystem - N
Framework For Global Supply Chain Ecosystem - N
Understanding the Role of Information Technology in Logistics and Supply Chain - N

modules.title: OPERATIONS AND INFORMATION MANAGEMENT FOR PROJECT MANAGERS
modules.summary: The aim of this unit is to develop a critical understanding of managing operations and information systems within projects. The interrelationships within functional areas will be examined as the influence of contemporary factors. Learners will explore organisational strategy in relation to the capacity to plan for products and consider the value of inventory management using information systems and inventory schedules.

lessons.title: Role of Operations in Business Management - N
Strategic Capacity Planning in Project Management - N
Introduction to Scheduling In Supply Chain Operations - N
Operations and Information Management for Project Managers

modules.title: ADVANCED RESEARCH METHODS
modules.summary: The unit aims to equip learners with the practical, technical, and methodological skills to conduct independent research for their research project and management broadly defined. It recognises that conducting research requires the development of specific and generic research skills, including understanding the research design process, understanding different techniques for conducting research in business and management studies, and appreciating the ethical and social implications of undertaking high-value research.
